idea-plugin.name: Mobiscout
idea-plugin.description:
Mobiscout - Intelligent Mobile Testing Platform

Point the IDE at a running app and get the artifacts a tester needs — a per-screen element inventory, the app's interaction graph, and runnable tests — into a new or existing framework, without leaving the IDE. Local-first: the engine runs on your machine, no servers.

Key Features:

  • 📱 Device Management - Control Android emulators and iOS simulators directly from IDE
  • 🔍 UI Element Inspector - List the current screen's elements and copy or generate a ranked locator for any of them
  • 📊 Live Device Logs - Stream logcat/simctl logs in real-time
  • 🎯 Interactive Control - Tap the device screen from the IDE, mirrored live
  • 🧠 Ranked, self-healing selectors - accessibility-id → resource-id → text, with fallbacks; element types from a hybrid ML + heuristic classifier
  • 🔄 Interaction Graph - the app's navigation map, mined into multi-step, form-filling test paths, with structural findings (unreachable / dead-end screens)
  • 🌍 Multi-Language - generate tests in Python, Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, C# or Maestro (pytest / TestNG / JUnit / WebdriverIO / NUnit / YAML flows), imperative or BDD, flat files or Page-Object structure
  • 🔌 Backends - Appium (Android UiAutomator2 + iOS XCUITest) and on-device Espresso
  • 🔐 Gates - pass login, TOTP/2FA, biometric, QR/document-scan and permission prompts to test behind them
  • ➕ Only what's new - generate tests only for what your existing suite doesn't already cover

Requirements:

  • For Android: Android Studio's SDK and an emulator or a connected device. Crawling over adb needs nothing more; Appium-mode crawls and running the generated kit need Node + Appium (npm i -g appium, then appium driver install uiautomator2).
  • For iOS (macOS): Xcode and a simulator, plus Node + Appium with the xcuitest driver (iOS crawls and kits run through Appium/XCUITest).

No separate engine to install — Mobiscout sets up its own local engine automatically on first use. Appium (above) is the one external tool the generated tests run against; the plugin tells you if it isn't reachable rather than failing silently.

Getting started:

  1. Open View → Tool Windows → Mobiscout.
  2. Connect a device or boot an emulator.
  3. Point it at your app and generate a test kit.

Docs at the repository; questions and bugs via GitHub Issues.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0 — first stable release

  • Engine + plugin reach 1.0 together. Point the IDE at a running app and get a per-screen element inventory, the interaction graph, and runnable tests — in Python, Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, C# or Maestro, imperative or BDD, flat or Page-Object.
  • Smoother first run. The one-time engine download now shows progress on the tool-window auto-start, so a slow first download no longer looks like a hang.
  • Publish polish. Trimmed change-notes, refreshed the feature list, and removed the last deprecated IntelliJ API usages.

0.14.0 — senior kits, source/API tests, security scanning

  • Generated kits rewritten to a senior bar. Page-Object suites by default for Python, Java, Kotlin, WebdriverIO and C# (new), with BDD on page objects (pytest-bdd/Behave, Cucumber, Reqnroll) — from one model, not flat scripts.
  • One suite for Android + iOS. The two platform models merge into a single cross-platform suite; the platform is chosen at run time.
  • Tests that fail until the app is fixed. Crashes and error screens become failing defect tests; negative-form and robustness tests ship by default.
  • API tests from a crawl alone via network capture, plus SwiftUI read from the Swift AST for more accurate iOS locators and navigation.
  • Active API security scanning (security api --active): SQLi, XSS, path traversal, auth bypass, rate limiting and CORS — opt-in, authorized and rate-limited; off by default.
  • Resilient runs: a crashed session costs one test, not the run; one target failing never costs the others.

0.13.3 — crawl quality + source-first graph

  • Interaction graph from source. New mobiscout source graph <dir> maps an app's screens and navigation straight from Android/Kotlin or iOS/Swift source — no device — as Mermaid / DOT / JSON, so you see the predicted structure before a crawl.
  • Dynamic lists no longer explode the crawl map. A scrolling feed/list was mapped as a new screen per row count; a list's length is treated as data now, so the crawl reaches real screens instead of near-identical list states.
  • Appium starts itself from the CLI too. crawl --driver appium now auto-starts Appium (with ANDROID_HOME) like the IDE already did, instead of failing with "No Appium server reachable".
  • Faster Android-over-Appium crawls via an adaptive settle on native screens, plus a safer negative-form probe and a Rust core on PyO3 0.29.
